lens: Mantine v8 full component kit: complete SaaS dashboard, rich forms, spotlight search
name: Mantine Coaching Console
one_liner: A Mantine v8 command console: a dark live-coaching cockpit, a job-based persona library, and a four-step AI persona wizard, applied across all nine screens.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the lens: one Mantine v8 kit (AppShell, Stepper, Tabs, Accordion, RingProgress, Drawer, Dropzone, Notifications, @mantine/charts) across all nine screens, with Spotlight as the global search and command bar. Deviated where research pushed: Mantine defaults read as a generic template, so the live call uses a fixed dark console and a custom token set. Mobbin and competitor evidence favours dual-channel waveforms, criterion chip scorecards and stepper wizards (Vapi, Grain, HubSpot, Jasper). Mobbin search was web-only, so mobile patterns are reasoned, not sourced. Self-scores (1-10; F3 where 1 = clearly worth it): A 8, B 8, C 7, D 5.6, E 5.2, F1 6, F2 7, F3 3.

ui_stack.name: Mantine v8 core
ui_stack.role: Single component system for the whole app: AppShell, Stepper, Tabs, Accordion, Drawer, RingProgress, Badge, Alert, Table, Chip, SegmentedControl
ui_stack.why: 120+ components and 70 hooks cover the dashboard, forms and wizard; native CSS styling is easy to override with our tokens; dark mode via defaultColorScheme.

ui_stack.name: @mantine/spotlight
ui_stack.role: Global Ctrl+K search and command bar
ui_stack.why: Grouped action lists and a fuzzy filter map directly to searching personas, scenarios, debriefs and actions like 'Build persona from this JD'.

ui_stack.name: @mantine/charts (recharts)
ui_stack.role: Score trends, criteria radar, sparklines, readiness
ui_stack.why: Charts inherit the Mantine theme, so we do not hand-style recharts on every screen.

ui_stack.name: @mantine/form + existing zod schemas
ui_stack.why: Keeps the zod contracts the repo already uses for scenarios and rubrics.

ui_stack.name: @mantine/dropzone and @mantine/notifications
ui_stack.role: Upload of JDs, CRM notes and call transcripts; toasts and mic-permission prompts
ui_stack.why: Native to the kit, so the wizard does not need a second upload library.

ui_stack.name: @tabler/icons-react
ui_stack.why: Mantine's default family; 1.5 stroke reads well at 18px in dense consoles.

ui_stack.name: Geist + Geist Mono via next/font
ui_stack.role: UI and display type; tabular numerals for timers and scores
ui_stack.why: Distinct from default Inter/Sora look, with clean numerals for live scores.

ui_stack.name: Kept: Next.js 15, React 19, @elevenlabs/react, OpenAI Realtime, Prisma/Postgres, zod, three.js
ui_stack.why: Only the UI layer changes; three.js is lazy-loaded for the voice orb only.

ui_stack.name: Dropped: Tailwind 3 and globals.css component classes
ui_stack.role: Removed after each route is ported
ui_stack.why: One styling system instead of two.

palette.use: Live console and dark-mode page background
Primary text on light; body text meets AA
Rep actions and focus ring; white label passes AA at about 5.4:1. Use #8C9BFF for links on dark
Persona channel on dark and strong scores. On light, text uses #0E7F62 for contrast
Whisper cues and provisional score state; dark text on amber backgrounds
End and grade button and objection alerts on light; use #FF7A8C text on dark

design_language.typography: Geist for UI and display: headings 600 with -0.02em tracking; body 15px/1.5 on desktop and 16px on mobile. Geist Mono with tabular figures for timers, scores and transcript timestamps. Loaded via next/font/google.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 10px radius on controls, 16px on cards, pill chips. Depth comes from 1px hairlines and surface steps (canvas, surface, raised). Shadows only on floating elements such as Spotlight and Drawer. The live console is always dark, even when the rest of the app is in light mode.
design_language.motion: Mantine transitions for Drawer and Spotlight at 150-200ms. Score bars ease over 400ms and delta arrows flash once. Waveform is canvas-drawn at about 30fps and pauses when the tab is hidden. Under prefers-reduced-motion, bars become static and the orb is replaced by a still persona avatar.
design_language.iconography: Tabler icons through @tabler/icons-react at 1.5 stroke, 18px inline and 20px in navigation. Icons always pair with a text label on mobile.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default for library, briefing, debrief, dashboard and team. Dark is the default for the live call and README hero. Both use Mantine defaultColorScheme set to auto plus CSS variables for tokens; the console is fixed dark everywhere so live screens look identical.

navigation_and_ia: Replace the glass header with a Mantine AppShell: a collapsible left navbar on desktop (Home, Practice, Library, Create persona, Progress, Team, Settings) and a bottom tab bar on mobile (Home, Library, Practice, Progress, More). Ctrl/Cmd+K opens Mantine Spotlight across personas, scenarios, past debriefs and actions, with grouped results. Entry points converge on one path: Library card to Pre-call briefing to Live call to Debrief to Targeted re-run. Team and org routes appear only when an org is connected, so the solo open-source experience stays clean.

screens.layout: Full-width Stepper at the top: Source, Persona, Scenario, Dry run. Step 1: left column holds a Dropzone for files and a Textarea for pasted text or a URL; right column is a checklist of what will be extracted (role, buyer goal, objections, pricing stance) that ticks as inputs arrive. Steps 2 and 3: editable draft fields on the left, each with an AI badge and source-tag chips; a live buyer-view preview card on the right. Step 4: a 60-second dry run in voice or text, then Save to library or Download file. Drafts show Skeleton rows that fill in.

Middle: the last two turns in large type, with a tap to open the full transcript. The coaching cue sits in a bottom Drawer peek showing one amber line. live_coaching_and_scoring: Three layers on one dark console. Whisper strip: one amber cue above the composer (for example 'Ask for the callback number before quoting price'), visible about 4 seconds, with Settings for off, text-only or audio whisper. Talk-track Stepper: six steps from the scenario, ticked as the model detects each one. Live rubric: each criterion shows a provisional score bar, a delta arrow after every turn, and an evidence chip that jumps to the transcript line that moved it. Scores stay dimmed until two consecutive turns agree. Objection alerts appear as a rose Alert pinned to the transcript. The debrief reuses the same rows, so live and final numbers match. Per-turn grading uses the current default gpt-4.1-mini under a token budget, and falls back to the keyword heuristic with a visible notice.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: grouped sections by sales job covering SDR cold call, AE discovery, SaaS, insurance, mortgage, real estate, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success and collections. A left facet rail filters by role, industry, difficulty, objection type and channel, with counts; filter chips sit above the grid. Cards show a generated initials avatar (no photoreal faces), role, temperament meter, objection tags, and Preview or Practice. Wizard: a four-step Stepper (Source, Persona, Scenario, Dry run). Source accepts a job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP or a pasted call. Drafted fields stream in, each tagged with the source sentence it came from. Rubric weights must total 100, shown on a live bar. Save writes a persona file that can go into a pull request.
signature_moments: Whisper strip: one amber cue fades in above the composer and never blocks typing.
Evidence chips: every rubric movement links to the transcript line that caused it.
Ctrl+K Spotlight across personas, scenarios, debriefs and actions, including 'Build persona from this JD'.
Wizard fields stream in tagged with their source sentence, so users see where each persona detail came from.
Debrief 'Replay this moment' jumps the transcript and audio to the quoted line.
Model stack panel: each feature names its OpenAI model and shows cost per session.
openai_fund_angle: Make OpenAI visible and useful, not logo-stuffed. A 'Model stack' panel in Settings and the README shows which model runs each job: the OpenAI Realtime model for voice, gpt-4.1-mini (current default) for live cues and grading, and a larger GPT model for the persona wizard. Per-session token and cost chips let reviewers see real usage, and the landing page runs the live console on those calls. For contributors, every persona is a reviewable file, the wizard exports a PR-ready persona, and a root AGENTS.md plus a 'Contribute a persona' page explain how Codex CLI can draft and review persona pull requests. Use only OpenAI's official 'Powered by' assets under their brand guidelines.

inspirations.borrowed: Competitors' scored feedback arrives after the session, not live; SCORM/LTI and SSO are table stakes. This is the gap we can own. Vendor claim, not verified.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1: install Mantine v8 with postcss-preset-mantine, define the token theme, build AppShell and Spotlight, then remove Tailwind last. Phase 2: port Pre-call briefing and the live console behind a feature flag, leaving API routes, Prisma and the ElevenLabs and Realtime hooks untouched. Phase 3: ship the persona catalogue and wizard on a new JSON persona schema, seeded by contributors to 50+ personas. Phase 4: debrief, dashboard, team view and the mobile pass. Use screenshot diffs per route and keep Tailwind classes only until each route is ported.

risks: Mantine defaults look generic; without the custom token set and dark console the redesign repeats the template problem.
Live cues and scores can be wrong or unstable, and per-turn grading adds cost and latency that can break the feel of a call. Show provisional state, budget tokens and test on slow networks.
Persona quality and licensing: 50+ personas must be original, free of real-company names and copyrighted scripts, which needs a contributor guide and a review step.
Total rewrite of nine screens risks regressions in voice and text modes and in accessibility. Mitigate with feature flags and per-route screenshot diffs.
Free general chatbots are the baseline for many reps, so the open-source core must beat them on scoring evidence, not only on looks.

Enterprise competitors (Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli, Mindtickle, Gong) publish SOC 2 and LMS integrations; SaaS viability depends on hosted, compliance and LMS layers beyond the open-source core.
Mobbin search was web-only, so the mobile live-call layout is reasoned rather than sourced from mobile references.
Waveforms and colour-coded scores need text labels, shape cues and reduced-motion fallbacks to meet accessibility standards.
